_readme: Curated YouTube channels for the SEBI Grade A (IT) syllabus. Every channel URL below was checked to resolve. Playlists are linked as YouTube searches scoped to the channel rather than hard-coded playlist IDs, because playlist IDs get renamed and deleted while channels do not.
howto: Watch a lecture ONCE at 1.25x-1.5x, then close it and write the four main points from memory. If you cannot, rewatch that one section only.
Video is for topics that will not click from the notes. It is the slowest way to revise, so never use it for revision - use the notes and flashcards.
Cap video at about 45 minutes a day. Beyond that it becomes comfortable procrastination that feels like studying.
Always finish a video topic by doing 10 questions on it in the Question Bank. Watching without testing produces recognition, not recall.

groups.name: SEBI Grade A — exam-specific channels
groups.note: Start here for strategy, pattern and previous-year discussion. Treat coaching content as a supplement to the official SEBI material, never as a replacement for it.

items.t: Anuj Jindal — SEBI / RBI Grade A
items.d: The best-known channel for SEBI and RBI Grade A. Strategy, syllabus breakdown, previous-year analysis and free classes on securities market awareness.
Detailed sessions on SEBI Act, regulations and the securities market. Useful for Phase I Paper 1 and the interview.
Quant, reasoning and English sessions for bank/regulator exams, plus mock analysis.

groups.name: Securities market & finance — build the intuition
groups.note: You need to understand markets, not just memorise them. These make the concepts concrete before you read the regulation.

items.d: The regulator's own investor-education videos. Short, authoritative, and exactly the framing SEBI itself uses.
Exchange-side explanations of trading, settlement and market operations.
The clearest free explanation of markets, derivatives and trading mechanics in India. Pairs with the derivatives and secondary-market notes.
Beginner-friendly market and accounting basics. Good if the financial side feels foreign to you as an IT graduate.
Mutual funds, AIFs and personal-finance products explained simply.

groups.name: Operating Systems
groups.note: Highest-yield IT subject after security. Watch for scheduling, deadlock, memory and paging — the topics with numericals.

items.d: Short, exam-focused lectures that map almost one-to-one onto this syllabus. The single best match for the IT paper.
Long-form complete course. Use when a topic needs slower, fuller treatment.
Clean, structured English lectures. Best if you prefer a university style.

groups.name: Computer Networks
groups.note: Focus on the OSI/TCP-IP split, IP addressing and subnetting, TCP congestion control, and the application protocols.

items.d: Covers every layer with exam-style framing, including subnetting numericals.
Excellent on the data link layer, error detection and flow control protocols.

groups.name: DBMS & SQL
groups.note: Normalisation, transactions and SQL writing are the scoring areas. Practise SQL by typing it, not by watching it.

items.d: Normalisation and transaction/concurrency lectures are particularly good.
Worked examples on functional dependencies and candidate keys — the skill the exam actually tests.
Complete course if you want the subject built from scratch.

groups.name: Data Structures & Algorithms
groups.note: For the objective paper you need complexity, properties and behaviour more than implementation. Do not fall into a coding-interview rabbit hole.

items.d: The clearest algorithms teaching on YouTube. Greedy, dynamic programming and graph algorithms especially.
Structured DSA course in Hindi, with code.
Trees, hashing and sorting with worked traces.

groups.name: Programming — C, Java, Python
groups.note: The paper asks output-based and concept questions, not large programs. Watch enough to read code confidently.

items.d: Approachable Hindi courses in C and Python, good for pointers and memory.
Java, OOP, collections and multithreading explained simply.
Multi-hour complete courses in almost every language and technology.

groups.name: Computer Organisation & Digital Logic
groups.note: Cache mapping, pipelining and number systems carry the numericals. Boolean algebra and K-maps are free marks once practised.

items.d: Cache mapping and pipelining numericals worked step by step.
Boolean algebra, K-maps, combinational and sequential circuits.

groups.name: Software Engineering
groups.note: Mostly definitional. A single pass on video is enough; spend the saved time on security.

items.d: SDLC models, estimation, testing and project management.
Short lectures on COCOMO, testing and process models.

groups.name: Cyber Security, Cloud & Emerging Tech
groups.note: Your differentiating block. Use video for the concepts, then read the bundled NIST documents and SEBI's CSCRF — a panel will ask about the regulation, not the YouTube explanation.

items.d: Full courses on security fundamentals, cryptography and ethical hacking basics.
Symmetric and asymmetric cryptography, digital signatures, attacks.
Search-based: cloud service models, containers, blockchain fundamentals.

groups.name: Quant, Reasoning & English (Phase I Paper 1)
groups.note: These are habit subjects. Twenty minutes of daily practice beats three hours of watching.

items.d: Shortcut techniques, DI sets and sectional strategy for regulator exams.
Search-based: the reasoning topic that decides Paper 1 timing.
Search-based: error spotting rules and reading comprehension technique.
